newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon ceasefire agreement monitors meet.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon ceasefire agreement monitors meet.

text.p: A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in Lebanon met on Monday to look into a Lebanese complaint that Israeli gunners shelled a Lebanese village on Friday, wounding 10 civilians.
Representatives of the United States, France, Israel, Lebanon and Syria met in the village of Naqoura to discuss the complaint over the shelling of Safad al-Batikh village.
Israel said the bombardment was a reprisal for a mortar attack by pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas who fired from the village into Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
It was the most intensive shelling of a Lebanese village since a U.S.-brokered April 26 ceasefire understanding which ended a 17-day Israeli blitz of Lebanon aimed at crushing Hizbollah.
The understanding included an undertaking by Israel and its South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia ally not to shell Lebanese civilians and set up the committee to monitor compliance.
The understanding says Israel and Hizbollah are committed to ensuring that under no circumstances will civilians be the target of attack nor will civilian areas be the launching ground for attacks.
But it allows Hizbollah to attack Israeli troops in south Lebanon and allows Israel the right to self-defence.
